questions.questionText: Extract E (line 10) states: ‘The minimum efficient scale in the water industry is large’. With the help of a diagram, explain why the large minimum efficient scale in the water industry is likely to lead to the market being supplied by a few large firms with monopoly power.

Figure 5 shows the average revenue (AR), marginal revenue (MR) and marginal cost (MC) curves for an industry which was perfectly competitive but is now a monopoly. The cost and revenue curves remain unchanged. Which of the following areas shows the total deadweight loss of consumer and producer surplus resulting from the structure of the industry changing from perfect competition to monopoly?

Extract B (lines 9–10) states: ‘After the monopoly’s patent expires, other companies can manufacture and market the same drug under its generic name, usually at a lower price.’ With the help of a diagram, explain why prices of pharmaceutical drugs supplied by a monopoly are likely to be higher than in markets which are more competitive.

Figure 7 shows the average and marginal revenue (AR and MR) curves and the average and marginal cost (AC and MC) curves for a firm. The firm is in equilibrium producing an output of Qe. From the diagram it can be inferred that the
options: firm is a price taker and will reduce its supply if the market price falls below Pe.
firm is making abnormal profits but this will not attract new firms into the market because the firm has a monopoly.
firm is maximising its abnormal profit and has no incentive to expand its production.
firm’s abnormal profit will lead it to expand its production and shift its market supply curve to the right.

questions.questionText: Discuss whether governments should consider increasing the regulation and taxation of technology firms which have acquired significant global monopoly power.

Explain how the data in Extract A show that the market power of the Big Four banks is weakening against competition from smaller rivals.
A firm benefits from significant and persistent economies of scale as it increases output. Which one of the following is the most likely consequence as it grows in size? The firm’s
options: ability to set its own prices will increase.
long-run average cost curve will become ‘U’ shaped.
increasing profitability will attract many new entrants.
total cost of production will decrease.
